nfl.oneThing: The Steelers are moving on without Aaron Rodgers, with Mason Rudolph starting Friday against Denver after Rodgers was benched and then waived following a scorched-earth interview.

headlines.title: Steelers stand by McCarthy after Rodgers' exit
headlines.summary: The Steelers benched Aaron Rodgers on Tuesday night, with a team statement saying Rudolph will start Friday against the Broncos and Rodgers will be inactive. Rodgers then said on The Pat McAfee Show that he wouldn't return, and Pittsburgh waived him. In that interview he accused coach Mike McCarthy of sleeping through team meetings. Sources told ESPN and NFL Network that the Steelers are standing by McCarthy, and McCarthy said the decision to bench Rodgers was his, with ownership's support. Rodgers said he learned of the benching from teammate Pat Freiermuth.
headlines.whyItMatters: Pittsburgh is 6-4 and seventh in the AFC playoff picture, so Friday's game against Denver is the first test without Rodgers.

headlines.title: Kinchens ejected, Watson ruled out with a concussion
headlines.summary: Rams safety Kamren Kinchens was ejected in the second quarter at SoFi Stadium on Wednesday night after leading with his head into Packers receiver Christian Watson. Kinchens reached 18.41 mph on the play, and he is the first Rams player disqualified since Puka Nacua in 2024. Watson had four catches for 65 yards and his eighth touchdown of the season before leaving. He was ruled out for the second half. The teams went to the break tied 13-13, and the Rams later moved ahead 20-13 on a Blake Corum touchdown.
headlines.whyItMatters: Both teams are 6-4 and in the NFC playoff hunt, with the Packers seventh and the Rams just outside the top seven. Watson's 916 receiving yards are third in the league.

nba.oneThing: The Knicks have won six straight to move to 12–6, while the Cavaliers are almost certain to miss the NBA Cup knockout stage after a 121–102 loss to New York.

headlines.title: Knicks extend winning streak to six
headlines.summary: The Knicks beat Cleveland 121–102 at Madison Square Garden on Wednesday night. Jose Alvarado scored a season-high 21 points and Mikal Bridges had a season-best 19, as the bench led a blitz that outscored the Cavaliers 39–17 in the fourth quarter. Jalen Brunson scored 19 but shot 6-for-22, and the Knicks had trailed by 11 multiple times. Donovan Mitchell scored 30 and James Harden had 28 for Cleveland, which fell to 9–10. The Cavaliers are 2–2 in the NBA Cup, and the Knicks are the defending champions and the first team to win the Cup and the Finals in the same season.
headlines.whyItMatters: New York is third in the East at 12–6, while Cleveland is seventh at 9–10 and nearly out of the NBA Cup.

headlines.title: LeBron's first triple-double for the 76ers
headlines.summary: LeBron James had 25 points, 12 assists and 10 rebounds for his first triple-double with Philadelphia in a 111–104 NBA Cup win over Miami. Tyrese Maxey scored 30 to lead the 76ers, and the win ended the Heat's seven-game winning streak. James became the oldest player in NBA history to record a triple-double. The win also gave Philadelphia the top spot in East Group B.
headlines.whyItMatters: The 76ers are 15–4 and first in the East, while Miami is 10–7 and sixth.

headlines.title: Jaylen Brown out with hamstring tightness
headlines.summary: Jaylen Brown left Philadelphia's win over Miami with left hamstring tightness and was ruled out. Coach Nick Nurse said Brown would have imaging and the team would update his status on Thursday. The injury is a recurrence of a hamstring strain that first caused him to leave a game against Brooklyn, where he tied his season high of 31 points. He missed two games after that before returning to score 20 against Portland. Brown is averaging 22.4 points, 6.3 rebounds and 3.6 assists.

headlines.title: Austin Reaves back at Lakers practice
headlines.summary: Austin Reaves was a full participant at Los Angeles' practice on Wednesday after missing about two weeks with a bruised left heel. He said it felt like he had broken his foot. Reaves is the Lakers' second-leading scorer, but his status for Friday's game at San Antonio is still unclear.
headlines.whyItMatters: The Lakers are 15–3 and second in the West, level with the Spurs at the top. Reaves' availability could affect that game.

recaps.text: The Knicks trailed by 11 more than once and looked like they might drop a game that would have hurt their Cup hopes. The turn came in the fourth quarter when Alvarado, the backup, led a bench surge that outscored Cleveland 39–17. Brunson struggled from the field, but the depth carried New York to a result that keeps its Cup title hopes alive.

recaps.keyLine: Buzelis 24 pts, 5 reb, 0 ast · Giddey 12 pts, 11 reb, 7 ast · Miller 35 pts, 3 reb, 1 ast, 3 stl · Reid 18 pts, 8 reb, 2 ast
recaps.text: Chicago had the lead in the closing seconds, and Matas Buzelis made the difference with a tip-in and two free throws to push it to three. Brandon Miller answered with a layup, but Coby White's off-balance jumper rimmed out at the buzzer. The Bulls have now won two straight, while Charlotte has lost seven in a row.

Giannis Antetokounmpo had 32 points and 14 rebounds for the Heat, but it was LeBron James and Maxey who controlled the game for the home side. Jaylen Brown's injury is the main concern for Philadelphia after the game.

contextCard.title: How NBA tiebreakers work
contextCard.body: When teams finish level on record, the NBA settles the order with a set list of tiebreakers. Head-to-head results come first, followed by division and conference records and other measures. Because of this, the standings can shift quickly as teams play each other.
